fatal_errors: The proposal combines friction stir processing and pre-oxidation, so it does not identify a single intervention as requested.
It replaces the target Mo-containing Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite and Mo-content variation with unmodified coarse-grained CoCrFeNi and an unrelated surface treatment.
The predicted coefficient of friction below 0.3 over the entire 25–800 °C range is unsupported by the cited evidence and conflicts with the target system's pronounced friction maximum near 200 °C.
The experiment does not isolate the effects of nanocrystallization and pre-oxidation, making the proposed mechanism difficult to attribute even if performance improves.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of improving CoCrFeNi tribology over a wide temperature range and plausibly invokes oxide-glaze protection at high temperature. However, it does not reconstruct the paper's intervention: varying Mo from x = 0.2 to 1 in an SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite. It consequently misses Mo-induced lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, silver-molybdate formation, and the actual Mo0.2 baseline. Agreement is limited to testing in air up to 800 °C and the general role of protective oxides. The cited studies support fine-grain wear resistance and tribo-oxidation only in a general sense; they do not establish that friction-stir processing plus pre-oxidation will maintain friction below 0.3 from room temperature to 800 °C. The proposed 10–100 N range also differs substantially from the specified 8 N test and omits counterface, speed, and distance. The controlled comparison is partly falsifiable, but 'appreciably lower' is vague and the two coupled treatments prevent causal discrimination.
